why: One registry so that 'code exists', 'something was executed once' and 'an external project can adopt this' can never be averaged into a single flattering word.
rules: integration=ADOPTED requires a named external project running the surface, with evidence committed.
integration=PILOT requires a named external partner and a committed pilot record; a plan is not a pilot.
execution=EXECUTED means a committed artifact proves the call happened; it says nothing about adoptability.
code=BUILT_UNVERIFIED means the file exists but no test or executed artifact covers it.
No single combined label may replace these three axes anywhere in docs/.

surfaces.label: Stellar integration adapter (read / build / submit gate)
surfaces.note: Reads Horizon and builds intents; submission only through an injected submitter. No live integration, no customer.

surfaces.label: Soroban commitment anchor (contract + first commit call)
surfaces.note: Deployed to Stellar mainnet and commit() INVOKED by the owner's own script. No external project calls it.

surfaces.label: DEX gating against the real order book (DEX-GATE/1)
surfaces.note: Five verdicts computed against the live XLM/USDC book. Returns PLAN_ONLY; it never sends.

surfaces.label: Agent payment gate, policy matrix (STELLAR-AGENT/1)
surfaces.note: VERIFIED / REJECTED / HELD matrix executed offline; submit NOT_PERFORMED (credential-gated).

surfaces.label: Pre-sign authorization receipts (PSAR/1)
surfaces.note: A receipt binds an authorization decision to the exact transaction XDR bytes (sha256 + Ed25519 over canonical JSON), fail-closed PASS or BLOCK; every verdict carries executionProof NOT_INCLUDED. Offline demo: npm run stellar:presign. No wallet embeds it; the Freighter proposal is a proposal, not an integration.

surfaces.label: Agent payment gate + signed receipts + independent verifier (AGENT-GATE/1)
surfaces.note: The flagship surface: refuses an envelope that diverges from the authorized intent, including a batched second payment. No signer, no submission, no chain read. Distinct from product 1 of the agent-commerce family — the composed AC-FW/1 firewall (agent-authorization-firewall), which composes packages/policy over the agent-commerce verdict rather than extending this Stellar mandate gate.

surfaces.label: Freighter wallet wrapper
surfaces.note: No end-to-end test: there is no browser wallet in CI and no credential path. Credential-gated, not proven.

surfaces.label: Mainnet executor (payment / invoke / anchor)
surfaces.note: Returns PLAN_OK plus sample code. It is a planning surface, correctly labelled PLAN_ONLY.

surfaces.label: Independent receipt verifier (offline, no CoreGuard server)
surfaces.note: Verifies committed evidence packages; adoption by a third party is 0.

surfaces.label: Envelope builder and decoder (AGENT-XDR/1)
surfaces.note: Builds unsigned envelopes, decodes signed ones, refuses secrets, fee-bumps and unreadable bytes. An envelope carries no network: the hash binds the caller's passphrase. An envelope built here was signed and included on Stellar testnet (tx 7f863dd2…41b757, ledger 5665413) on 2026-11-10 and re-decoded offline.

surfaces.label: Freighter signing adapter
surfaces.note: Contract verified with an injected wallet: signed, empty, unsigned and swapped-bytes cases. The signing path also carried a real testnet signature to a ledger, but with a local keypair behind the Freighter interface — the extension was probed in the available browser and is NOT installed (window.freighter undefined), so a real extension has still never signed here. A real extension promotes this surface to BUILT by signing in the demo, which writes docs/evidence/agent-gate-freighter-extension-signature.json only after the server verifies an Ed25519 signature by the declared wallet key; node scripts/agent-gate-freighter-attest.mjs --verify re-derives it and --promote edits this registry.

surfaces.label: Third-party verifier CLI
surfaces.note: Exit codes 0/2/3/4 proven, including a receipt paired with a foreign envelope. Zero external users have run it.

surfaces.label: In-process performance measurement
surfaces.note: 2000 samples recorded. In-process only: not deployed latency, not chain confirmation, not throughput.

surfaces.label: Runnable browser demo (gate → wallet → conformance → receipt)
surfaces.note: A judge runs the local server and drives the loop in a browser. The page probes window.freighterApi and window.stellar.freighter, and when neither exists it says a local demo keypair signed rather than claiming a wallet. Nothing is submitted to a ledger.

surfaces.label: Agentic escrow arbitration adapter
surfaces.note: DRY_RUN / NOT_BUILT by design; structurally unable to claim a live call.

surfaces.label: People's Court attestation adapter
surfaces.note: Fail-closed intake only. A read-only review is not an integration, an endorsement or adoption.

surfaces.label: Agent Authorization Firewall (AC-FW/1) (product 1)
surfaces.note: Product 1 of the agent-commerce family as ONE composed face over the existing engines (packages/policy + the CGCR/1 consent binding + the CGEP/1 verdict + AGR/1 — no fifth engine): a request-time interception gate (authorizeRequest: committed policy against the declared request, consent byte-match, caller-pinned window, single-use replay consulted but never consumed) and the after-the-fact review (reviewExecution: the full verifyExecution record). Refusals carry the frozen AC-FW/1 codes; ALLOW requires an empty reasons list; decisions are byte-deterministic. TEST_EXECUTED (contract tests + deterministic demo with committed artifacts); integration NOT_BUILT (no external adopter yet). Distinct older engines it composes but does not absorb: packages/firewall (Phase-D EVM decision core) and packages/agent-gate (Stellar mandate gate, AGENT-GATE/1).

surfaces.label: Verifiable Consent Receipts (CGCR/1) (product 2)
surfaces.note: Product 2 of the agent-commerce family: a consent record binds the user's approval to the exact approved order bytes as an independently re-derivable receipt; a verifying execution that diverges is fail-closed INVALID with the drifted field named (AGR/1). Durable cross-process consumption anchoring on the same host is provided by the file-backed AC-CS/1 store adapter (consumedSet injection); an on-chain single-use marker remains OWNER-GATED / NOT_BUILT.

surfaces.label: Agent Risk Engine (AGR/1) + standalone CLI (product 3)
surfaces.note: Product 3 of the agent-commerce family: deterministic authorization-drift taxonomy (named classes + severities, classes frozen) plus standalone CLI with assessment persistence (`packages/agent-commerce/risk-cli.mjs`: JSON report + JSONL ledger). Not a probabilistic fraud score; VERIFIED ≠ SAFE.

surfaces.label: Agent Commerce SDK + MCP + REST API (product 4)
surfaces.note: Product 4 of the agent-commerce family: the commerce arc ships as SDK surface + MCP server (stdio JSON-RPC) + REST endpoints (POST /v1/authorize, POST /v1/verify, POST /v1/risk-assess). npm publication is owner-gated.

surfaces.label: Durable single-use consumption store adapter (AC-CS/1)
surfaces.note: File-backed Set-compatible consumption ledger for durable cross-process single-use anchoring on the same host via existing consumedSet injection. NOT a distributed ledger and NOT an on-chain marker; an on-chain consumption marker remains OWNER-GATED / NOT_BUILT. VERIFIED ≠ SAFE.

surfaces.label: Agent Commerce named attack battery (prompt-injection fuzz + post-approval swaps/drifts + replay + cross-session gap + expiry + tamper)
surfaces.note: Deterministic six-vector prompt-injection fuzz set, recipient swap post-approval, tax/shipping/fee escalation, credential substitution, replay, the DOCUMENTED cross-session consumption gap (fresh ledger cannot see prior consumption — named on the report, never hidden), expiry, receipt tamper, byte-determinism. Offline, synthetic orders only; VERIFIED ≠ SAFE.

surfaces.label: Agent Commerce TypeScript declaration surface (AC-SDK/1 typed façade)
surfaces.note: Type-only declaration surface over index.mjs + risk.mjs, validated structurally (declared value-exports ↔ runtime exports, constant equality, boundary strings, no implementation) and type-checked in CI via `npx --yes --package typescript@5.9 tsc --noEmit --project packages/agent-commerce` (declaration surface + smoke).

surfaces.label: Agent Commerce authorization-decisions & receipts dashboard (bilingual operator view)
surfaces.note: Arabic-first RTL page with an English mirror: decision timeline (APPROVE → EXECUTE exact → MCP INVALID → HTTP VERIFIED), the 8 named attacks refused, the consent receipt id + pinned epoch, and the honest gaps panel. Embeds the committed suite artifacts verbatim; fully offline (no external scripts, fetches, absolute URLs or imports).

surfaces.label: Cross-Chain Execution Attestation (CGXA/1) + Soroban consent-binding preparation (product 5)
surfaces.note: Product 5 of the agent-commerce family: one verifiable statement binding the consent receiptId + the executed-order commitment (the CGEP/1 trace-domain hash) + the target chain's COMMITTED binding record (frozen adapter registry: Core DAO anchor chainId 1116 per docs/DEPLOYMENT.md; Stellar anchor contract per docs/EVIDENCE-MATRIX.md) + verification level COMMITTED_EVIDENCE. Offline, deterministic, fail-closed with 9 frozen reject codes. Soroban consent-binding integration is BUILT as offline preparation (CGXA-SOROBAN/1: `buildSorobanConsentBinding`, commit_authorized invocation payload, no broadcast). THERE IS NO BROADCAST SURFACE — any commit_authorized call is owner-authorized only and NOT_PERFORMED; an attestation of one environment is never bridge trust or a relay; VERIFIED ≠ SAFE.
